summary: AUDPROC is a shared Audit Trail subroutine. Called with an audit request (who/what/before-and-after images/message), it appends one timestamped audit record to a sequential audit log file (opened EXTEND). It maps the caller's fields onto the audit record layout, writes it, sets the return code (0 success / 8 on write or open error), and closes the file. It is the common 'write an audit entry' service used across the system (e.g. by PORTMSTR after an update).

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CALL 1000-INITIALIZE
CALL 2000-PROCESS-AUDIT
CALL 3000-TERMINATE
RETURN to caller (GOBACK)

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
ACCEPT WS-FORMATTED-TIME FROM TIME STAMP
OPEN AUDIT-FILE for append (EXTEND)
IF open NOT success THEN DISPLAY error; SET LS-RETURN-CODE=8; CALL 3000-TERMINATE; RETURN (GOBACK) END IF
branches: IF audit-file open failed -> terminate + return

annotations.note: OPEN EXTEND = append mode; audit records are added to the end of the log, never overwritten.

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-AUDIT
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CLEAR AUDIT-RECORD
SET audit fields from the request: timestamp, system/user/program/terminal header, type, action, status, key info, before-image, after-image, message
WRITE AUDIT-RECORD
IF write NOT success THEN DISPLAY error; SET LS-RETURN-CODE=8 ELSE SET LS-RETURN-CODE=0 END IF
branches: IF audit write failed -> rc=8 else rc=0

annotations.note: Captures both before- and after-images — a full change record for audit/compliance.

usage.note: Produced by Claude Code in-session; no API call, no key, no token cost.
